_about: Design basis for the structural model. Every value here is an input you can change; run.py reads it each time. Units: kN, m, kPa (kN/m2). 'src' says where each value comes from.

concrete.src: R26 general notes (5 Oct 2026): C30/37 (cube 37 MPa), up from C25/30 in R10. Site pour orders say C35 / 35 MPa (lib/concrete/pourOrder.ts); as a cube strength that is about C28/35, run as a check.

steel.src: R10 general notes: high tensile H = 500 N/mm2

stiffness.src: Cracked-section modifiers in the usual range (ACI 318 6.6.3.1.1 / EN 1998-1 4.3.1(7) gives 0.5 for all); same model used for gravity and lateral

soil.src: R10 general notes: estimated bearing capacity 400 kN/m2 at 4.0 m depth, from the geotechnical investigation report

dead.src: 50 mm screed + tiles + soffit plaster 1.5, services 0.25 (common Ghana/UK practice); roof: screed to falls + waterproofing + terrace tiles 2.5

walls.src: Sandcrete block walls plastered both sides (Structville unit weights; Tarmac block data): 225 hollow 3.5 kN/m2 x ~2.9 m = 10 kN/m round the edge; internal 150 hollow walls (8-9 kN/m) spread as 2.5 kPa until the plan walls are read in as line loads (EN 1991-1-1 6.3.1.2(8) says walls over 3 kN/m should be line loads)

imposed.src: EN 1991-1-1 Table 6.2: dwellings 2.0, private balconies 2.5, stairs 3.0 (cat A range 2-4), accessible roof/terrace 2.0; seismic mass psiE = phi x psi2 (EN 1998-1 4.2.4): 0.15 floors, 0.3 roof

stairs.src: 175 mm waist + 150/250 steps, on plan; tiled

pool.src: 1st floor sections (rev. 10 Oct 2026): 300 mm suspended pool slab between B1-C and 4-7, 0.9 m deep at grid 4 sloping to 1.35 m from 5 to 7 (1.2 m average), 200/300 mm pool walls on 600x950/750/600 beams and 950x300 columns below; walls modelled as 1850 x 300 deep beams

lifts.src: Machine-room-less lift: rail/car/counterweight reactions at the top of each shaft, typical 8-person lift; replace with the supplier's figures

roof_tanks.src: None in the record yet: add {x_mm, y_mm, kN} for each water tank on the roof

wind.src: Ghana Building Code Part 5 Table 5.8: Accra 29 m/s 3-s gust (50 yr), converted to a 10-min mean of about 20 m/s for EN 1991-1-4; terrain category III (suburban); torsion e = b/10 (EN 1991-1-4 7.1.2)

seismic.src: Ghana Building Code: Accra in zone 3, ag = 0.35 g (hazard studies give 0.06-0.2 g at 475 yr; 0.20 g run as a sensitivity). EN 1998-1 type 1 spectrum, envelope of ground types B and C until Vs30 is measured; importance class II; DCM dual system q = 3.0 (3.6 if regular; 2.0 if torsionally flexible -- checked by the model)

combinations.src: EN 1990 Eq. 6.10 (STR), 6.12b (seismic), characteristic SLS for bearing pressures

zones.name: 700 base on line C (C1a at C/5, C/7)
700 base on line G (C6 at G/5, G/7)
700 base on line L (C6 at L/5, L/7)
700 base on line M (SW7, C1b at M/7)

ground_loads.name: basement wing B-E
ground_loads.src: basement finishes 1.5 + suspended ground floor slab and beams over it 6.0 + ground floor finishes 1.5 + 300 mm retaining walls (90 m) spread 9.0; storage 5.0 + parking 2.5

extra_loads.name: underground water tank C-D/3-5
extra_loads.src: R10/architect: tank inside 300 mm RC walls, 2.5 m of water assumed

700.src: H25@75 top and bottom both ways (98-H2504@75 T2/B2, 4x46-H2502@75 T1/B1)

450.src: H16@150 top and bottom both ways (48-H1605/H1606, 84-H1613)

beam_links.src: RAFT BM 550x300 along every grid line F-N, H10 links (H1001, 3850 No.); 2 legs x 4 arms through an interior column, spacing assumed 150

raft.level_note: As built (Niko, 19 Nov 2026): the raft is founded on bedrock about 2 m down on average, shallower than the drawing's 2.95 m to the raft top plus 1 m of stabilisation. Raft underside about -1.7 to -2.0, top about -1.2 to -1.5; the model puts the raft at the ground floor level, with the fill between as a load on it.
raft.src: Updated raft details (18 Feb 2026): foundation layout, setting out, sections 01-01 and 03-03, raft details sheet 1 and rebar seats. 450 mm raft in the basement wing (B-E) inside 300 mm retaining walls, 500 mm raft F-N with 550x300 raft beams on every grid line, 700 mm bases under the lift cores and on lines C, G, L and M round the heavy columns. Zone edges read off the 1:100 plan and tied to the as-built grid (the plan's row spacings are the earlier ones).
raft.k_src: Rock: modulus of subgrade reaction 150 MN/m3 for weathered rock (Bowles: k ~ 40 x q_ult; dense sands 64-128, rock above 200). Replace with the geotechnical report's figure; the check stays on the geotech's 400 kPa as a conservative bearing limit.
raft.ground_src: Over the 500 mm raft: about 1.35 m of earth (19 kN/m3) and 0.3 m hardcore (21) up to the 150 mm ground slab (3.75) plus finishes 1.5 = 37 kPa; parking 2.5 kPa

shown_at_mm.src: For the 3D view only (the analysis keeps the raft at the ground floor). Raft top -1.35 (ground floor slab +0.300): as built on bedrock about 2 m down, underside about -1.7 to -2.0. Basement floor -2.20: as built the basement is about 2.3 m high inside (site, 20 Nov 2026), up to the underside of the 200 mm ground floor slab at +0.100; so the basement steps down 0.85 m from the rest of the raft (the drawings had it 2.95 m below the ground floor).

foundation.src: type 'raft' (full raft on soil springs) or 'pads' (columns fixed at +0.300, pad sizes worked out)

basement.src: Updated raft details (18 Feb 2026) foundation plan: 450 mm raft inside 300 mm RC retaining walls on grids B and C from the stair north of row 2 to row 7, and round the water tank C-D / 3-5 (walls on centre lines of the as-built grid); the architect's basement plan (A103): storage, stair, water storage. Section 03-03: 150 mm ground slab on 300 mm hardcore over the fill elsewhere.
basement.water_note: Water drawn 2.0 m deep, under the 2.3 m basement height; the analysis's tank load (extra_loads, 2.5 m of water) is on the safe side.

flat_slab.src: 2nd floor punching shear details (rev. 12 Oct 2026): 250 mm flat slab G-N, column strips with H12@100 links (H1201, 919 No.) both ways through every column; legs per perimeter assumed 8 (2 legs x 4 strips)
